name: Michael R. Stoddard
current_role: Certified public accountant and government auditor
bio: Michael Stoddard is the Libertarian Party nominee for Utah's 3rd Congressional District, with a campaign based in Orem. He is a certified public accountant and certified financial planner who graduated from Brigham Young University and says he has spent decades auditing municipal and state governments.

platform.point: Require rotating independent outside audits of federal finances and personal certification of statements by top Treasury and budget officials.
Open the Federal Reserve to an independent external audit and return money-creation power to Congress.
Repeal legal-tender rules so other currencies can compete and end capital-gains taxes on gold and silver.
Create an after-tax savings account of up to $10,000 a year and index asset gains and interest for inflation.
Equalize tax treatment of individual health spending, allow cross-state catastrophic plans, and require up-front pricing.
Opposes federal and state efforts to disarm citizens, citing Virginia's semi-automatic rifle ban as an example.
Restore state-controlled militias separate from the Guard and limit federalized Guard use in domestic law enforcement.

economy.evidence: Proposes tax-free savings accounts, inflation indexing of capital gains and interest, ending taxes on gold and silver gains, and ending legal-tender rules.

welfare.evidence: Proposes market-based health reforms such as cross-state catastrophic insurance and direct primary care, with open, direct public funding only for people who cannot get coverage.

liberty.evidence: On guns, opposes disarmament at the federal and state level, including Virginia's semi-automatic rifle ban; no stated positions found on abortion, drugs, LGBTQ rights or speech.

security.evidence: Proposes repealing federalization provisions so the National Guard is kept out of domestic policing except in narrow constitutional cases.

foreign.evidence: Opposes undeclared wars and overseas Guard deployments without a formal congressional declaration of war.

notes: The campaign site was found through the Libertarian Party of Utah's candidate page, and scores come from its position papers. No statements were found on immigration, energy, tech, education or religion, and web search was unavailable for news coverage.

name: Ayden Scott
bio: Ayden Scott is an unaffiliated candidate for Utah's 3rd Congressional District in 2026.
notes: Checked the Utah candidate filing list, the Wikipedia race page and likely campaign domains; no website, social accounts or issue statements were found. Web search was unavailable in this pass, so news coverage could not be checked.

name: Taylor Wright
bio: Taylor Wright is the Libertarian Party nominee for Utah's 4th Congressional District. He is a physical education teacher who also works extensively with adults with special needs. He took part in an April 2026 debate with fellow 4th District candidates Steven Burt and Seth Stewart.

platform.point: Says government should not distort markets or burden consumers through policies such as tariffs.
Favors peace, trade and diplomacy over military intervention, and respect for other nations' sovereignty.
Wants Congress to reclaim its constitutional role in checking executive power, especially on war.
Wants many responsibilities now held by Washington moved to states, communities and individuals.
Says free people and free markets can produce better solutions to save the Great Salt Lake.

economy.evidence: Opposes tariffs and government distortion of markets, and campaigns on limiting federal power.

foreign.evidence: Opposes military interventions as wasteful and favors trade and diplomacy, though this is stated in general terms.

notes: Reviewed every campaign page and post and the state Libertarian Party page; the April debate exists only as a video (https://www.youtube.com/live/2sjjQOVQUuQ) with no transcript. His individual-liberty statement names no specific issues, so liberty and most other topics remain unscored.

name: Steven Burt
bio: Steven Burt is an unaffiliated candidate for Utah's 4th Congressional District from South Jordan. He is an attorney with nearly 20 years of practice who has spent about a decade as an in-house lawyer and executive in the solar industry, and says he has done pro bono immigration work.

platform.point: Names rising costs and stagnant incomes as his top priority under the heading of restoring the American Dream.
Calls the immigration system broken and wants ICE refocused on finding and deporting dangerous criminals.
Stresses federalism, limited government, separation of powers and the rule of law.
Runs unaffiliated and says the two-party system should end.
Says members of Congress should live in their districts and focus on constituents' needs.

immigration.evidence: Says ICE is out of control and should be redirected toward deporting dangerous criminals as part of broader reform.

notes: Reviewed the campaign site's pages and blog feed; the 'Our America', 'Declare Your Independence' and wildfire pages contain only embedded documents or headings with no readable positions. The April 2026 debate video has no transcript, so most topics remain unknown.

name: Ahsen Malik
bio: Ahsen Malik is an independent candidate for Virginia's 10th Congressional District; his name appears on the ballot as Ahsen Mujeeb Malik. A Virginia native and University of Virginia graduate, he is a middle school teacher with past work in residential mortgage finance and real estate.

platform.point: Supports single-payer coverage for all Americans, through either state-run Medicaid-for-all or federal Medicare-for-all.
Supports a secure border plus permanent legal residency, without citizenship, for undocumented immigrants; opposes mass deportation.
Proposes a federal right to abortion through 15 weeks with a later ban, except when the mother's life is at risk.
Backs local bans on new data centers and proposes a federal siting act to manage their costs.
Supports a bipartisan bill expanding clean energy, with a federal fast lane for clean-energy transmission permits.
Opposes the war with Iran that began in February 2026 and wants it ended quickly.
Supports a single binational state with equal rights and citizenship for Palestinians.
Pledges to push for a balanced federal budget as the long-term answer to inflation.

welfare.evidence: Supports a single-payer health insurance system covering all Americans, run either by states or through federal Medicare-for-all.

liberty.evidence: On abortion, backs a guaranteed right through 15 weeks with a federal ban afterward except to protect the mother's life; no stated positions found on drugs, LGBTQ rights, guns or speech.

immigration.evidence: Supports permanent legal residency for undocumented immigrants, higher legal immigration quotas and an end to mass deportation, while also backing border security.

foreign.evidence: Wants a smaller global US military footprint and opposes the Iran war, while also calling for cooperation among major powers and respect for international law.

energy.evidence: Supports a bill that aggressively expands clean energy and permitting reform that favors clean projects over fossil fuel infrastructure.

tech.evidence: Supports local bans on new data center construction and federal legislation to manage their effects, including required site disclosure before construction.

notes: Positions come from the campaign site's issue pages. His balanced-budget pledge does not fit the economy scale, and no statements were found on security, education or religion; the headshot is embedded in the page and has no separate URL.

name: Dianne Blais
bio: Dianne Blais is the Green Party nominee for Virginia's 11th District and a longtime Fairfax County volunteer who has served as state co-president of both the League of Women Voters and AAUW. She convenes the Jane Addams branch of the Women's International League for Peace and Freedom and is active with World Beyond War. She was the Green nominee in the 10th District in 2014 and ran as an independent for the House of Delegates in 2011.

platform.point: Adopts Ralph Nader's Compact for America, including a $15 minimum wage.
Supports higher taxes on the wealthy and on corporations.
Supports Medicare for All.
Wants money spent on wars and war preparation redirected to needs at home.
Lists open borders among her goals.
Calls for a moratorium on data centers.
Supports free public transit.
Supports ranked-choice voting.

economy.evidence: Backs a $15 minimum wage and, in general terms, higher taxes on the wealthy and corporations.

welfare.evidence: Supports Medicare for All and free public transit.

immigration.evidence: Lists open borders as one of her goals.

foreign.evidence: Wants spending on wars and war preparation redirected to domestic needs, and opposes trying to force other countries to follow US wishes.

energy.evidence: Cites environmentalism as a core value and calls for a green US, a general statement without specific energy policies.

tech.evidence: Calls for a moratorium on data centers.

notes: Her campaign site was found through the Wikipedia race page; scores come from its 'What I Stand For' page. Her call for 'improved incarceration' was too vague to score, and no statements were found on social issues, education or religion.

name: Geral D. "Bishop" Staten
bio: Geral D. "Bishop" Staten is an independent candidate on the ballot for Virginia's 2nd Congressional District and has run for local office in Suffolk. News reports say he is running on the Democratic Socialists of America platform, though the local DSA chapter says it is not affiliated with him. In September 2026, Democratic nominee Elaine Luria sued the state elections department to challenge his ballot petition signatures.
notes: Checked the Wikipedia race page, Virginia Scope, the Virginia Political Newsletter (mostly paywalled) and FXBG Advance; reports mention a DSA platform but none describe specific policies, so nothing could be scored. No campaign website was found, and his Facebook activity is not readable without logging in.

name: Joan Andrews Bell
bio: Joan Andrews Bell is an independent candidate for Virginia's 4th District and a longtime anti-abortion activist who has been arrested many times at clinic protests. She was convicted under the federal FACE Act in 2023 and pardoned by President Trump in January 2025. Her candidacy is part of the Defending the Unborn slate of independent congressional candidates.

platform.point: Campaigns against later-term abortion in Virginia.
Urges voters to reject Virginia's Amendment 1 abortion-rights ballot measure.
Uses her candidacy to air television ads showing images she says depict abortion's victims.
Presents opposition to abortion as a civil rights cause, comparing it to the fights against slavery and segregation.

liberty.evidence: Campaigns against abortion and Virginia's Amendment 1; no stated positions on drugs, LGBTQ rights, guns or speech.

notes: Listed on the ballot as Joan E. "Andrews" Bell; her campaign site and the babies.vote slate page cover only abortion, so the liberty score rests on that issue alone. No statements were found on any other topic.
